authority: ADVISORY request budget. It sizes how long a scheduled lane's in-process cloud call waits for its answer. It never authorizes spend, selects a provider, raises a process cap or narrows the routing policy.

measurement.window: 2026-11-01T13:00:00Z <= created_at < 2026-11-08T13:00:00Z (fixed bounds, so a re-measure is reproducible; do not use now()-relative)
measurement.rows: success = true only: a row cut at the old budget is censored at that budget and cannot measure the tail
measurement.population: model_lane = 'grok' for each process_id: the lane's slow shared path, which every cron-mode call can be routed to. A blend over all providers understates the tail -- the Anthropic promotion answered 1251 of topic_ingestion's calls in 4.0 s p95 while its grok path ran 20.6 s p95.
measurement.why_capped: the grok proxy spawns one hermes child per request with a 240 s timeout, so a caller budget above 120 s only lengthens a wait that is already failing; 120 s is also the value the keepalive probe adopted (LQ-750, fold step 30)
measurement.recheck: re-derive from this file alone with `python scripts/lib/llm_lane_budgets.py --report` (no DB, exits 1 on drift); re-measure p95_ms/max_ok_ms from llm_consumption_log with the same window and population when re-sizing. The unit test re-computes every row from p95_ms/max_ok_ms and fails if this file drifts from its own method
